concerns.text: T025 (Feature Integration) depends on T024 (Fidelity Loss Calculation). T024 is listed under User Story 2 (Feature Engineering), but FR-003 and US-3 define 'dimensional fidelity loss' as the TARGET variable for the predictive model (US-3). Calculating the target variable in US-2 creates a semantic dependency violation where the target is generated before the model training context (US-3) is established, confusing the separation between feature engineering and target definition required for a valid regression setup.

T022b computes a 'Global Dominant Eigenvalue' as a single scalar constant for the entire dataset. T025 merges this constant into every per-sample record. However, FR-002 and US-2 imply sample-level entanglement scores. If the 'entanglement score' is a global constant, it cannot serve as a predictor variable in the Random Forest (which requires a feature vector per sample) to predict sample-level fidelity loss, rendering the model training (FR-004) logically impossible as described. The task order implies a feature that is mathematically invalid for the intended regression.

T030a (Permutation Test) and T030c (Null Baseline) are ordered such that T030c depends on T029 (Evaluation), but T030a also depends on T029. However, SC-002 requires a 'paired t-test' against the null baseline to verify statistical significance. T030c only implements training a mean predictor and comparing metrics; it does not include the t-test logic. The task order places the validation of SC-002 (T030c) before the final integration (T031), but the task description for T030c is insufficient to satisfy the success criterion, creating a gap where the required validation step is missing from the execution flow.

T001d is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but explicitly depends on T001a (Directory Creation). While T001a is in the same phase, the [P] tag implies no dependencies. This is a minor semantic inconsistency in the parallelization tag, though the explicit DEPENDS clause clarifies the actual order.
